family.tagline: Grandchildren for the summer, photos at home, and a Core by the window.
family.story: Gunnar is a portrait photographer. Ngozi is an operations consultant. Both work from home, in a white house by the canal. Their clients' files sit on one Companion Core.

companion.name: Tobe
companion.job: Opens Twenty and other web pages in its own browser and fills in the forms Gunnar asks for.
companion.limits: One task at a time. Gunnar checks every result.

companion.name: Linnea
companion.job: Drafts replies and answers questions for Ngozi's clients, using the context she connected.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Ngozi reads and sends every message.

popup.title: A parcel at the door
popup.body: A parcel waits at the Lindqvist-Abara front door. Gunnar carries it through the dining room to the study, where Ngozi clears a space on the desk.

popup.title: Unbox the Companion Core
popup.body: Inside: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. The Core's footprint is about three quarters of a sheet of paper.

popup.title: Plug it in
popup.body: Ngozi plugs in the power cable and presses the button. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Join it from a phone
popup.body: Gunnar opens the Wi-Fi settings on his phone and joins the Core's own network. Then he chooses the home network from the list.

popup.title: Pick your first agents and apps
popup.body: In Companion Hub, Ngozi picks Hermes, Gunnar picks OpenClaw, and they add Immich and Nextcloud. Companion Memory (beta) comes along. Then they walk away.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Linnea says hello
popup.body: Ngozi messages the agent she named Linnea. Linnea answers, and the Core is running.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: mika
say.text: Hello, Ngozi. I am Linnea. What should we do first?

beats.capability: back up, search and organise your family photos and videos

popup.title: Photos land on the Core
popup.body: Gunnar backs up the weekend's photos to Immich from the couch. They land on the Core, ready to search and organize.

beats.capability: stream your own movies, shows and music to every screen in the house

popup.title: Film night, from the Core
popup.body: Friday is film night. Jellyfin streams Ngozi's own collection of movies to the living-room TV, straight from the Core.

beats.capability: a shared grocery list, recipe book, meal planner

popup.title: One list, two phones
popup.body: Gunnar and Ngozi share the grocery list in KitchenOwl. Oat milk added at the counter shows up on the other's phone.

beats.capability: a shared grocery list, recipe book, meal planner

popup.title: Grandma's soup, kept
popup.body: Gunnar types his grandmother's soup recipe into KitchenOwl once. Now it sits in the family recipe book, beside the meal planner.

beats.capability: track every subscription you pay for and get a reminder before it renews

popup.title: Every subscription, in one list
popup.body: Ngozi opens Wallos at the counter. It lists every subscription the household still pays for, with a reminder before each one renews.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: A draft, never sent alone
popup.body: A client asks a tricky question. Ngozi texts Linnea, and Linnea drafts a reply using the context Ngozi connected to Companion Memory (beta). Ngozi reads it and sends it herself.

say.speaker: mika
say.text: Here is a draft. Please read it before you send it.

beats.capability: scan and file your paperwork; it reads every page, tags it and makes it searchable

popup.title: Paper in, searchable out
popup.body: Ngozi scans a supplier invoice. Paperless-ngx reads every page, tags it and files it, so a search finds it later.

beats.capability: a password vault you host that works with the Bitwarden apps

popup.title: Passwords stay in the house
popup.body: Ngozi opens VaultWarden, the password vault for the household. It works with the Bitwarden apps, and the vault itself lives on the Core.

beats.capability: your files, calendar and contacts on your own Core, synced to your devices

popup.title: One calendar for both of them
popup.body: Shoots and client calls land in one Nextcloud calendar. Ngozi and Gunnar see the same week on their phones.

beats.capability: design and prototype in a web-based design tool you host

popup.title: An album, laid out at home
popup.body: Gunnar lays out a client's album in Penpot, a web-based design tool hosted on the Core. Each spread comes together in his browser.

beats.capability: keep customers, deals and custom fields in a CRM you host yourself

popup.title: Tobe logs a new enquiry
popup.body: A new portrait enquiry arrives. Gunnar asks Tobe, and Tobe opens Twenty in its own browser to add the lead. Gunnar checks every field.

say.speaker: elias
say.text: Lead added. Please check the details.

beats.capability: merge, split, compress and convert PDFs on your own Core

popup.title: Quote and contract, one file
popup.body: Gunnar merges a quote and a contract into a single PDF with Stirling-PDF. The merge runs on the Core.

beats.capability: track your plants, watering and care history across rooms and beds, with photos and a garden journal

popup.title: The new hedge has a journal
popup.body: Ngozi logs the new hedge in HortusFox. She notes where it grows, when she watered it, and adds a photo for the journal.

beats.capability: stream your own music collection to any device

popup.title: Music by the pool
popup.body: Gunnar plays his own music collection from Navidrome on the patio. It streams from the Core to his phone.

popup.title: One Core, a whole household
popup.body: Photos, paperwork, lights, cameras and two agents. The Lindqvist-Abara household runs it all from one Companion Core in the study.

closing.body: Your photos, your paperwork and your agents can run on a Companion Core at home. Browse the Companion Hub store and pick your first apps.

notes: Exemplar written by the showrunner. FTUE beats follow the owner's hotspot flow (STORY-BIBLE section 8); owner sign-off against the fact sheet is open.
ftue-hello and office-reply show Hermes over a chat service; the disclosure note is on the first Hermes beat.
garden-cameras assumes the family owns an IP camera: it is not in the Core box and not in the 3D scene.
